rationale: B wins by being the tighter editor. Its best move is folding the door-count news into a real protagonist angle, "Sephora more than doubles its Glossier footprint to 1,400 doors," while A spins the same terrain into a standalone "Glossier more than doubles its retail footprint" angle and a broader Kohl's "test case" that starts to smell like trend furniture. A's fragrance-retail angle is useful, but B's refusals and proof demands are cleaner: fewer shiny objects, less invented scaffolding.
gaps_in_A: "Sephora at Kohl's becomes a test case for prestige beauty in a big-box mall" overreaches. The update says Sephora at Kohl's is included; it does not prove a big-box prestige-beauty test case or an already-covered channel story.

"why scent, unlike skincare or makeup, is a category that historically underperforms in pure DTC" may be true, but it is not in the supplied facts. A flags the causal gap later, but the angle still leans on outside category logic.

"Glossier more than doubles its retail footprint" is useful trade news, but as a standalone angle it is thinner than B's retailer-protagonist version. Door count alone is not much of a second paragraph.
The two Kohl's angles are defensible but adjacent: "Sephora at Kohl's" as channel test and "Kohl's shoppers" as access story need sharper separation or one will eat the other in pitching.
gaps_in_B: B misses the strongest way to use the fragrance fact. Refusing "Glossier launches three new fragrance products" is right, but it never offers A's better combined retail-sampling angle.
"The beauty brand born on a blog is coming to Kohl's" uses "cult brand's positioning" without that fact in the update. That's a small but unnecessary reach.
"Twelve years from beauty blog to 1,400 retail doors" is the softest kept angle. Without principal access, it becomes a company-history feature no editor asked for.

"what Sephora gets from it and which shelf space it displaces" is a good reporter question, but shelf displacement is not supported by the update and needs to stay framed as a question, not a premise.
